title: SELF-LEADERSHIP, DIGITAL LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES, AND INNOVATIVE BEHAVIOUR: AN INTEGRATED ANALYSIS
summary: This study examines the relationships among self-leadership, digital leadership competencies, and innovative behaviour. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 210 managers working in organisations undergoing digital transformation. Confirmatory factor analysis compared a correlated seven-factor model with a theoretically specified second-order model. The second-order model showed acceptable but marginal fit ([Formula: see text]; CFI [Formula: see text] 0.890; TLI [Formula: see text] 0.878; RMSEA [Formula: see text] 0.071) and did not fit significantly worse than the seven-factor model. In the theoretically specified model, self-leadership was strongly associated with innovative behaviour ([Formula: see text]), self-leadership was associated with digital leadership competencies ([Formula: see text]), and digital leadership competencies were associated with innovative behaviour ([Formula: see text]). Common-latent-factor analyses, however, showed that the latter two associations were sensitive to common method variance concentrated in the adapted digital competency measure. The findings therefore provide qualified evidence of association rather than mediation, moderation, or causality. The study contributes an integrated measurement assessment while identifying the need for independent validation and multi-source measurement of digital leadership competencies.

title: VI Encuentro Internacional de Investigación en Economía Solidaria e Innovación Social
summary: This publication brings together academic contributions and research experiences presented at the VI International Meeting on Solidarity Economy and Social Innovation (ESIS 2026), held from October 27 to 30, 2026, at the Universidad Cooperativa de Colombia, Santa Marta campus. Focusing on the social and solidarity economy, social innovation, and the development of solidarity-based territories, the publication explores alternative development approaches aimed at collective well-being, environmental sustainability, civic participation, and the strengthening of community organizations. The contributions are organized into six thematic areas: public policies, socioecological transitions, and active citizenship; solidarity-based territories and sustainable territorial development, with an emphasis on community-based tourism; entrepreneurship ecosystems, social innovation, and digital transition; education, research, and pedagogies for transitions; measurement of social, economic, and environmental impact; and solidarity-based food systems, agroecology, and sustainability. Through interdisciplinary perspectives, case studies, methodological proposals, and territorial experiences, the chapters examine topics such as cooperativism, community governance, economic inclusion, digital transformation, artificial intelligence, solidarity-based education, environmental management, and social impact assessment. Overall, the publication contributes to dialogue among academia, social organizations, and communities, fostering reflection on collaborative economic models capable of addressing contemporary social, environmental, and technological challenges.

title: Exploring Directions for ESG Executive Coaching Based on the ESG Implementation Experiences of Third-Tier Supplier CEOs
summary: This study aims to explore how CEOs of third-tier suppliers perceive and experience ESG management, and to derive practical directions for the ESG coaching they need. Three third-tier supplier CEOs from various domestic industries were selected as participants, and data collected through semi-structured interviews were analyzed using inductive content analysis. The analysis revealed that participants’ experiences converged into four themes: ‘Survival,’ ‘Lack of Implementation Capability,’ ‘Psychological Burnout,’ and ‘Accompanying.’ Participants perceived ESG not as an autonomous strategic choice but as a survival issue tied to the termination of transactional relationships, and faced psychological burnout from safety-related anxiety, generational and technological gaps, and severe emotional labor amid a lack of personnel and systems. What they genuinely needed was not one-off training but continuous support that acknowledges their emotional exhaustion and facilitates on-site implementation. Based on these findings, this study confirms the need to expand ESG support beyond one-way education into coaching interventions, and proposes a four-stage ESG coaching model: cognitive restructuring, problem-solving-oriented implementation coaching, emotional recovery coaching, and continuous accompanying. This study holds significance in deriving concrete directions for ESG coaching grounded directly in the implementation experiences of lower-tier supply chain CEOs.

title: ANALISIS IMPLEMENTASI E-GOVERNMENT DALAM MENINGKATKAN KINERJA PELAYANAN PUBLIK PADA DINAS KEPENDUDUKAN DAN PENCATATAN SIPIL KOTA DENPASAR TAHUN 2023–2025
summary: Digital transformation in public services has encouraged local governments to develop service systems that are faster, more accessible, and more efficient. This phenomenon can be observed at the Department of Population and Civil Registration of Denpasar City, which developed various digital service channels while maintaining mobile outreach services during 2023–2025. This study aims to analyze the implementation of e-government in improving public service performance at the Department of Population and Civil Registration of Denpasar City. The study employs a descriptive qualitative method using documentation and secondary data analysis derived from performance reports, policy documents, and official information on population administration service innovations. The analysis covers service channel diversification, performance achievement, budget efficiency, accessibility, data integration, and organizational capacity. The findings show that e-government implementation is carried out through Taringdukcapil, the Anjungan Dukcapil Mandiri (ADM), and JB Pelangi. This implementation has been accompanied by an increase in population and civil registration document ownership coverage from 99.34% in 2023 to 99.79% in 2024, while maintaining the Public Service Index at an A category. However, challenges remain, particularly digital literacy gaps and the need to strengthen cross-agency data integration. Therefore, e-government has contributed positively to public service performance, but its development needs to become more inclusive and integrated. Keywords: e-government, public services, population administration, digitalization, Denpasar City

title: Transformasi Perilaku Konsumen Halal di Era Digital: Peran Islamic Branding dan Customer Engagement terhadap Repurchase Intention
summary: Digital transformation has reshaped halal consumer behavior, particularly in information searching, brand interaction, and repurchase decisions. In an increasingly competitive halal industry, companies must strengthen both Islamic brand identity and digital customer engagement to build customer loyalty. This study examines the effect of Islamic branding on halal product repurchase intention, with customer engagement as a mediating variable. A quantitative survey was conducted involving 150 Muslim consumers in Indonesia who had purchased halal products online. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS. The results show that Islamic branding has a positive and significant effect on customer engagement and repurchase intention. Customer engagement also positively and significantly influences repurchase intention and mediates the relationship between Islamic branding and repurchase intention. These findings indicate that Muslim consumers demonstrate stronger repurchase intentions when halal brands provide emotional attachment, positive digital interactions, and a strong Islamic identity. Theoretically, this study integrates Islamic branding, customer engagement, and repurchase intention within the Islamic marketing and digital consumer behavior literature. Practically, halal businesses should optimize social media, develop relevant Islamic content, and improve digital customer experiences to strengthen engagement and loyalty.

title: TECHNOLOGY ADAPTABILITY AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AMONG SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES IN UGANDA
summary: Digital transformation has become an important driver of business competitiveness, operational efficiency, innovation and sustainable enterprise development. For small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in developing economies such as Uganda, the capacity to adapt to emerging technologies is increasingly important for business survival and participation in the digital economy. However, despite the expansion of mobile telecommunications, digital financial services, electronic commerce and government-supported digitalisation initiatives, many Ugandan SMEs continue to experience difficulties in integrating digital technologies into their business operations. This integrative critical literature review examines the relationship between technology adaptability and digital transformation among SMEs in Uganda, focusing on technological readiness, organisational capabilities, managerial competencies, financial resources, institutional support and environmental influences. The review draws on established theoretical and empirical literature, including the Technology–Organisation– Environment framework, Technology Acceptance Model, Diffusion of Innovations theory, Dynamic Capabilities theory and Resource-Based View. It critically examines the extent to which these frameworks explain technology adoption and sustained digital transformation within resourceconstrained enterprise environments. The synthesis identifies interconnected barriers involving inadequate digital competencies, limited access to affordable financing, infrastructure constraints, cybersecurity concerns, organisational resistance and uneven access to digital markets. It further highlights opportunities associated with mobile money, cloud computing, digital marketing, electronic payment systems, enterprise management applications and emerging artificial intelligence technologies. The review argues that technology adaptability should be understood not simply as the willingness to adopt technological innovations but as a multidimensional organisational capability involving continuous learning, strategic flexibility, technological integration and institutional responsiveness. It concludes that successful digital transformation among Ugandan SMEs depends on the interaction of internal enterprise capabilities and supportive external conditions.

title: Restructuring Corporate Governance in the Critical Minerals Sector to Strengthen Indonesia's Economic Sovereignty in the Global Value Chain
summary: Changes in the global economic structure have placed critical minerals in a strategic position because they are needed in the development of electric vehicles, batteries, energy networks, low-carbon technologies, and various strategic industries. Indonesia holds a key position in the global value chain for critical minerals, particularly nickel. However, high mineral production in a country does not necessarily indicate that the country controls the economic value generated along the production chain. Differences between resource location, corporate ownership, technological mastery, financing, and market access indicate issues that cannot be resolved solely through mining or trade policies. This study analyzes the construction of corporate governance for critical minerals in Indonesian law, its role in strengthening the capture of Indonesia's economic value in global value chains, and the need for corporate governance reconstruction to strengthen economic sovereignty. The study uses a normative juridical method with legislative, conceptual, case, and comparative approaches. Primary legal materials consist of Indonesian laws and regulations, Constitutional Court decisions, World Trade Organization documents, and relevant international instruments. Secondary legal materials come from scientific literature and publications from the OECD, IEA, and UNCTAD. The research findings indicate that Indonesian law has provided the basis for state control over mineral resources, mining operations, investment, and corporate governance, but has not yet integrated the strategic character of critical minerals into a corporate governance framework that specifically addresses economic sovereignty. This research proposes the concept of Strategic Mineral Corporate Governance, which encompasses ownership transparency, strategic responsibility of corporate organs, supply chain risk management, due diligence, technology development, domestic value capture, sustainability, and accountability. This reconstruction is not directed at restricting foreign investment, but rather at establishing governance that can enhance domestic capacity and Indonesia's position in the global value chain while still adhering to international business law.

title: Sustainable internationalisation of African higher education: African strategies, global lessons and epistemic justice
summary: Introduction African higher education is increasingly being shaped by globalisation, digital transformation and sustainability demands. While internationalisation can expand access, research capacity, quality assurance and global partnership, it may additionally reinforce inequality, cultural homogenisation and epistemic dependency when poorly governed. This study therefore reframes internationalisation as a sustainable governance process grounded in African priorities and informed by global experience. Methods The study employs an integrative policy and practice review supported by qualitative document analysis and comparative thematic synthesis. Sources were purposively selected for their relevance to the research questions, and these included African and international higher education scholarship, policy models and institutional initiatives, primarily published between 2004 and 2026, with earlier works retained where conceptually necessary. Deductive and inductive coding was used to identify recurring patterns, tensions and adaptation risks, followed by comparative synthesis across African and selected international settings. Results The synthesis generated five interrelated dimensions for sustainable internationalisation in African higher education, which are digital inclusion and innovation, reciprocal partnerships, quality assurance and cross-border standards, human capital development, and cultural sovereignty with epistemic justice. Their integration reflects recurring themes relating to access, institutional authority, capacity development, quality and epistemic recognition. The framework translates these dimensions into institutional mechanisms and measurable indicators for implementation and monitoring. Discussion The study argues that sustainable internationalisation in African universities should engage with global higher education as active knowledge producers, while adapting lessons from Europe, Asia and the Americas to African institutional realities and development priorities. The study contributes a framework that positions internationalisation as an integrated governance process through which digital access, partnership, quality, institutional capacity and epistemic authority can be addressed collectively. The framework provides a foundation for future empirical application and comparative assessment across diverse African higher education settings.

title: Using artificial intelligence in insurance: ZhongAn Company as a case study
summary: Subject. Application of artificial intelligence technologies in the operations of the Chinese internet insurance company ZhongAn – the first professional online insurer in China. Objectives. To conduct a comprehensive assessment of the impact of artificial intelligence technologies on the operational efficiency of the insurance company and to identify factors limiting the full realization of the potential of digital transformation. Methods. The study employed comparative analysis of operational indicators for 2019–2024, trend analysis of the dynamics of investments in research and development, financial analysis of performance indicators, SWOT analysis, and content analysis. Results. It has been established that the automation of the insurance company’s key business processes through artificial intelligence has reached extremely high levels: the underwriting automation rate is 99%, the reduction in claims settlement time is 87.5%, and employee productivity has increased 30‑fold. A paradox of efficiency has been identified: the growth in operational performance is accompanied by a persistently high level of consumer complaints, the opacity (non‑interpretability) of algorithms, risks of homogenization, and a shortage of personnel. A similar phenomenon has also been observed in the Russian insurance market. The hypothesis has been confirmed that technological efficiency alone is not a sufficient condition for sustainable profitability and consumer trust. Conclusions. For Russian insurers, ZhongAn’s experience demonstrates the need for the simultaneous development of technological infrastructure, human capital, and a customer‑oriented culture. The key success factor is the transformation from a technological pioneer into a responsible leader by ensuring the transparency of artificial intelligence systems and striking a balance between innovation and trust.

title: Leading in the Digital Age: Investigating the Impact of Project Managers’ Digital Leadership on Construction Project Performance
summary: Abstract In the digital era, reshaping project leadership has become a strategic imperative for enhancing project performance. While digital leadership is gaining academic attention as an emerging paradigm within construction management, its impact on project outcomes and the underlying mechanisms remain empirically underexplored. Drawing on dynamic capability theory, this study aims to explore how the digital leadership of project managers relates to construction project performance. We propose a moderated mediation framework that considers team digital capabilities as a critical mediator and team identification as an important contingency of the mediation effect. Data were collected via structured questionnaires distributed to industry practitioners with direct experience in digital construction projects. Using structural equation modeling, we empirically tested our hypotheses based on responses from 343 seasoned project professionals. This study revealed a specific pathway wherein project managers’ digital leadership exhibited a positive link with project performance via the mediating role of team digital capabilities. Furthermore, team identification positively moderated both the direct relationship between digital leadership and team digital capabilities, and the indirect relationship between digital leadership and project performance through team digital capabilities. This study provides novel empirical evidence on the effectiveness of project managers’ digital leadership and how it translates into performance gains in construction projects, thereby enriching leadership and project performance research in the field of construction management within the context of digital transformation. It also offers project managers and team members a clear, practical path to promote construction project performance by actively cultivating team identification and systematically developing team digital capabilities.

title: Business Model Innovation Under Institutionalized ESG Regulation: An Ontological Account of Paradox Closure
summary: ABSTRACT Institutionalized environmental, social, and governance (ESG) regulation is reshaping how firms justify value, responsibility, and viability across industrial value chains. This paper examines how Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive requirements enter business model innovation in SMEs embedded in five industrial value chains. Drawing on a 3‐year longitudinal qualitative study of 25 SMEs, the findings show that ESG was initially treated as an external layer associated with documentation, compliance, and customer demands. When translated into business model reasoning, ESG surfaced persistent tensions among economic, environmental, social, and governance logics. These tensions were frequently closed through sequencing, commensuration, deferral, and compliance‐oriented reasoning. Artifact‐mediated workshops were associated with moments of provisional copresence, while the wider analysis identified governance constraints arising from the separation of ESG responsibility and decision authority. Building on these patterns, the paper advances the abductively grounded proposition that assumptions embedded in dominant BMI frameworks may reinforce ontological closure under institutionalized ESG conditions. It introduces the E 2 SG Flower as an analytically grounded paradox‐navigation proposition whose effects and transferability beyond the studied industrial value chains require further empirical validation.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Designing Digital Auditing Programs
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) plays a significant role in various aspects of life, including the design of digital auditing software for the Bank of Baghdad. This involves utilizing AI technologies to enhance audit procedures and improve the efficiency and effectiveness of auditors within the modern banking environment. The importance of this research stems from the expanding role of AI and digital transformation in the banking sector, which has compelled the auditing profession to adopt modern tools and techniques capable of handling vast amounts of financial and accounting data with speed and accuracy. A descriptive-analytical approach was adopted to address the theoretical aspects of AI and digital auditing software, alongside an applied approach to examine the actual implementation of AI technologies in designing the digital auditing software at the Bank of Baghdad. Data were collected through interviews, documentation, and online sources, then analyzed using appropriate statistical measures to assess the nature of the relationships and impacts between the study variables. The researcher reached several conclusions, most notably that AI has a direct impact on the design of digital auditing software by enhancing capabilities in risk assessment, financial data analysis, and the detection of potential errors and anomalies. Furthermore, AI contributes to increasing the efficiency of audit procedures and reducing the time and effort required to execute them. The results also indicated that the use of AI applications improves the quality of audit evidence and the reliability of the auditor's findings, thereby positively influencing the quality of financial reports and bolstering confidence in them. The researcher recommended expanding the use of artificial intelligence technologies at the Bank of Baghdad and providing the necessary technical infrastructure to support their applications. He also advocated for training auditors in the use of digital auditing tools and updating supervisory policies and procedures to align with the requirements of the modern digital environment and international auditing standards. Furthermore, the researcher emphasized the importance of establishing regulatory and professional frameworks to ensure the effective and secure use of artificial intelligence in digital banking audits.

title: Beneficial Ownership, Transparency and Corporate Governance in Uganda's Extractive Sector
summary: The extractive sector exploits resources that, under the Constitution, belong to the people, and generates revenues of great importance to development; yet the companies that hold extractive rights may conceal the natural persons who ultimately own and control them behind chains of intermediate companies, nominees and trusts, with consequences for taxation, for the fight against corruption and for the accountability of the sector. This article examines beneficial ownership, transparency and corporate governance in Uganda's extractive sector. It sets out the concepts of beneficial ownership, transparency and corporate governance and the reasons they matter in the extractive context; it traces the problem of corporate opacity to the principle of separate legal personality and examines the limited jurisprudence on piercing the corporate veil, in Salomon v Salomon, Gilford Motor Co v Horne, Adams v Cape Industries and Prest v Petrodel; it examines the international framework, comprising the EITI Standard, the FATF Recommendations and the United Nations Convention against Corruption; and it examines Uganda's legal framework, comprising article 244 of the Constitution, the Companies Act Cap 106 and its beneficialownership register, the Anti-Money Laundering Act Cap 118, the Public Finance Management Act Cap 171, the Mining and Minerals Act and the Petroleum (Exploration, Development and Production) Act, and Uganda's membership of the EITI. It argues that Uganda has a legal framework substantially aligned with international standards, but that its effectiveness is constrained by weaknesses of verification, enforcement, capacity and accessibility, and it recommends the strengthening of the register, of the institutions, of international cooperation, and of the governance of the companies, including the Stateowned extractive entities, in the sector.

title: Bridging circular economy standards and continuous improvement: the role of institutional pressures and digital technologies in firms' circular transition
summary: Purpose This study investigates whether and how the availability of circular economy (CE) standards supports firms' circular transition by fostering their orientation towards adopting CE practices and enhancing continuous improvement (CI). It further examines the moderating role of institutional pressures and the adoption of digital technologies in these relationships. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Institutional Theory, the paper develops and tests a conceptual model using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Empirical data were collected through a survey administered to non-circular-born firms. Findings Findings show that CE standards availability positively affects both firms' orientation towards adopting CE practices and CI. Firms' orientation towards CE practices also positively influences CI. However, the indirect effect of CE standards availability on CI through firms' orientation towards CE practices is not significant, suggesting that, in non-circular-born firms, standards may operate primarily as direct cognitive and operational infrastructures. Institutional pressures positively moderate the relationship between CE standards availability and firms' orientation towards adopting CE practices. Digital technology adoption exerts a direct positive effect on CI and positively moderates the relationships between CE standards availability and CI, as well as between firms' orientation towards adopting CE practices and CI. Originality/value The paper advances the emerging literature on CE standardisation by showing that standards should be understood not only as codification and measurement devices, but also as organisational enablers of continuous improvement. In doing so, it integrates research on CE standards, CI, digital transformation and institutional pressures, offering new evidence on how circular transition unfolds in non-circular-born firms.

title: Dynamic Graph Learning for Core Data Asset Discovery Using Data Lineage Graphs
summary: The rapid growth of the digital economy has made the accurate identification of Core Data Assets (CDAs) increasingly important for enterprise data governance. Existing approaches, however, often rely on static, homogeneous dependency modeling or node-centric analysis, limiting their ability to capture complex value propagation patterns and the structural importance of data in enterprise business processes. To address these limitations, this study proposes a graph learning framework with dynamic (structure-adaptive) edge weighting for automated CDA discovery using data lineage graphs. The framework first introduces a dynamic edge-weighting mechanism that integrates node influence and relationship scarcity to represent heterogeneous value propagation between data entities. The framework then constructs a comprehensive feature representation by combining global influence, local topological characteristics, and functional connectivity patterns, enabling the model to capture different aspects of data-table importance. Based on these representations, we develop an ensemble learning model with group-based cross-validation and automated hyperparameter optimization for robust CDA classification. Experiments on five real-world lineage graphs from a single enterprise data warehouse demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness. The model achieves average AUC and F1 scores of 0.926 and 0.753, respectively, and outperforms the evaluated baseline methods in terms of F1-score and Precision; the strongest competing baseline attains higher AUC and Recall but substantially lower Precision and F1-score. The results show that the multidimensional structural features provide the main share of the improvement, that the dynamic weighting mechanism contributes a modest additional benefit, and that the approach is effective for lineage graphs of moderate scale in enterprise data governance.

title: CLIMATE LITIGATION AS A REGULATORY COMPLIANCE TOOL: EXPANDING STATE AND CORPORATE RESPONSIBILITY
summary: The challenge of climate change poses significant regulatory and governance issues which are not limited to the conventional environmental law enforcement systems. International systems like the Paris Agreement set high mitigation levels but their success is heavily grounded on national implementation and accountability systems. Here, climate litigation has become one of the growing weapons of enforcement of regulatory compliance and increase of state and corporate responsibility. This study looking at climate litigation as a doctrinal and normative process that converts aspirational climate pledges into enforceable legal requirements. Through a qualitative approach to the doctrines, the research examines prominent cases of the judicial courts, international legal tools, and legal arguments to understand how the judicial courts perceive the constitutional provisions, statutory requirements, and human rights provisions in climate-related cases. Close emphasis is put on landmark cases like Urgenda Foundation v. The Supreme Court of the Netherlands ruled in the Netherlands v. Milieudefensie et al. and the District Court of The Hague ruled in Royal Dutch Shell v. Milieudefensie et al. which exemplify the increase in the judicial control over governmental climate policy and corporate emissions strategies. The results show that climate litigation acts as a supplementary regulatory compliance tool through three main directions, clarifying legal responsibilities, strengthening the correlation between national regulations and international climate policies, and creating wider corporate standards of care based on the human rights and due diligence principles. Climate change is becoming a justiciable matter by the courts, which reduces the distance between political obligations and legal responsibility. Litigation on the corporate level helps to create the climate-related governance through the impact on the reduction of emissions, disclosure of risks, and long-term sustainability planning. According to this study the climate litigation is a trend in environmental governance with a major change towards polycentric and multi-level accountability. In spite of institutional and procedural constraints on judicial intervention, judicial intervention is essential to sealing the enforcement gaps and supporting the legal framework of climate responsibility. Finally, climate litigation should not be viewed as a simple response-driven system of dispute resolution, but a new regulatory tool that is transforming the scope of state and corporate climate responsibility

title: Judicial Identification of Labour Relationships in Platform Work in the Digital Economy
summary: The development of the digital economy has reshaped the way labour is organised. Platform-mediated work - food delivery, ride-hailing, live streaming and on-demand freight - has expanded rapidly. Platform enterprises typically present themselves as providers of technical services, information matching or cooperative contracting, yet in practice they shape the labour process through algorithmic dispatching, service ratings, pricing rules, reward and penalty mechanisms and account control. The central judicial question that arises is whether a labour relationship exists between the worker and the platform or its partner enterprise. The traditional identification of labour relationships rests on personal, economic and organisational subordination, but platform work combines formal flexibility with substantive control, which gives rise to inconsistent standards across courts. Taking the notion of ‘dominant labour management’ as its point of departure, this article examines the doctrinal basis, the practical difficulties and the adjudicative approach to identifying labour relationships in platform work. It argues that the digital economy has not altered the essential structure of domination and subordination within the labour relationship; it has merely transformed labour management from direct commands into rule-based, algorithmic and evaluative forms of control. Judicial practice should adhere to a fact-first principle and assess, in combination, the contractual label, the work rules, algorithmic dispatching, the source of remuneration, business integration, the allocation of risk and the parties’ evidential capacity, so as to balance the protection of workers’ rights against the vitality of the platform economy.

title: Empirical Evaluation of Corporate Governance Practices on Sustainable Business Practices in Nigeria
summary: The focus of this research is the modeling of corporate governance for the attainment of sustainable business practices in Nigeria. The importance of corporate governance on achieving sustainable business practices especially in a developing country like Nigeria can not be overemphasized. The research design used in this study was the cross-sectional survey design, associated with the deductive approach used for descriptive research purpose, which was used to model the impact of corporate governance on sustainable business practices in Nigeria. This study analyzed the impact that corporate governance had on indicator variables of sustainable business practices such as: Environmental and Regulatory Framework, Good Corporate Citizens, Codes of Business Ethics, Stake Holders Treatments and Accountability of Officers. The findings elicited from this revealed that corporate governance recorded a positive impact on sustainable business practices in Nigeria within the scope of this study.

title: Circularity in pigment, resin and coating supply chains: a structured evidence synthesis and decision framework
summary: Purpose This study aims to critically review and synthesize how circular-economy mechanisms can be applied to pigment, resin and coating supply chains while preserving formulation performance and chemical safety. It asks which material and supply-chain mechanisms are supported, when they deliver environmental and economic benefit, and which governance and digital conditions are required for implementation. Design/methodology/approach A structured narrative review was conducted using Crossref, Google Scholar, publisher platforms and backward citation searching. Thirty core evidence records published through 2025 were retained after a citation-level relevance audit. Sources were classified by sector directness, evidence design, geographical context, technology maturity, functional unit or decision boundary and reporting transparency. The manuscript reports the complete search syntax and includes the full evidence extraction in the appendix. Because historical query-level exports were not retained, identification and screening counts were not retrospectively reconstructed. Findings The quantitative evidence is case-specific. In one Italian comparative LCA of two paints, a waste-paint option reduced assessed impacts by approximately 48% on average under the study assumptions. A separate Italian cradle-to-gate study of 21 mural paints reported 1.03 ± 0.60 kg CO2-eq per kg paint and an upstream contribution above 70%. In a global inventory-based coating study using annual world coating demand as the functional unit, epoxy resin, TiO2, acrylic resin and metallic zinc dust together contributed more than 53% in most ReCiPe 2016 categories; direct coating manufacture and most downstream processes were outside that boundary. Circularity therefore depends on performance retention, restricted-substance control, collection quality, verified virgin-material substitution and context-specific LCA–TEA rather than recovery rate alone. Originality/value The review differs from generic circular-supply-chain reviews and narrower coating reviews by mapping pigment characteristics, resin and coating performance, reverse logistics, LCA, TEA, hazardous-substance governance and digital traceability into a single evidence-derived decision sequence. The framework is a synthesis for prospective application, not an independently validated industrial model; its gates and measurable criteria are made explicit and illustrated with a waste-paint remanufacturing example.

title: Development Financial Literacy of the Population in the Digital Economy: the Role of Public Administration
summary: The relevance of this study is driven by the unprecedented growth in bank account frauds against the backdrop of financial services digitalization, which necessitates a review of public administration approaches in this domain. The objective of the study is to identify the interrelation between citizens' level of financial literacy and the effectiveness of state policy measures aimed at protecting their interests. Additionally, it seeks to determine promising directions for governmental activities to ensure a secure financial environment in contemporary Russia. The study analyses the Strategy for Improving Financial Literacy and Developing Financial Culture Until 2030, approved by the Russian Federation Government in 2023, as well as its implementation roadmap. It identifies the need to refine state regulatory measures aimed at combating the rising incidence of financial frauds. The author analyzes the results of researches on the level of financial literacy of Russians conducted by the Central Bank of Russia and the analytical center «National Agency for Financial Research» in 2017–2025. Principal result is the identification of vulnerable groups most susceptible to financial scams. The study identifies the categories of individuals most susceptible to financial fraud (risk groups). The scientific novelty of the findings lies in demonstrating a direct correlation between citizens' level of financial literacy and the effectiveness of existing approach to state regulation. The practical significance of the findings lies in the proposed mechanism of targeted influence on risk groups through the conduct of video consultations by state-owned banks. The recommendations formulated in the article can be included in the implementation roadmap of the Strategy for Improving Financial Literacy and Developing Financial Culture Until 2030.

title: ECONOMIC INVERSION IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: IMPLICIT INTANGIBLE ASSETS AND THE TRANSFORMATION OF CORPORATE VALUE
summary: The economic nature of implicit intangible assets is examined, and the concept of economic inversion of value is substantiated as a manifestation of the transformation of the sources of corporate value creation in the digital economy. Current trends in changes in the structure of companies’ market value and the sectoral distribution of intangible assets are analysed. Contradictions arising between classical financial theories and contemporary business valuation practices are identified. The economic essence of implicit intangible assets is revealed, and their role in the formation of competitive advantages and the growth of companies’ market value is determined. The author’s definitions of the concepts of "economic inversion of value" and "implicit intangible assets" are proposed. A conceptual model is developed to illustrate the interrelationship between the digitalisation of the economy, the increasing dominance of intangible capital, and the need to transform approaches to accounting and business valuation.

title: When Good Deeds Become Assets: An AI-Enabled Management Control and Accounting Governance Framework for the Erosion of Workplace Spirituality
summary: As AI-enabled workplace monitoring expands, organizations may increasingly have the technical capacity to classify prosocial conduct, assign scores, and link those scores to managerial incentives. This paper treats the governance implications as an AI-enabled management control and accounting governance question, not an engineering scoring study; reward crowding-out is borrowed evidence, not a new finding here. It makes two contributions. First, it explains how accounting measurement, target setting, budgeting, disclosure, and compensation design turn a fleeting motivational reaction into a durable arrangement reproduced across reporting periods. Second, it analyzes the asymmetry between auditable behavioral indicators and moral costs that resist measurement, and why those costs stay out of ordinary records. A four-arm governance design—management control, financial reporting, internal audit, compensation—extends these contributions in practice. Three layers and four falsifiable propositions follow, offered for later testing, not validated causal claims.

title: From Goals to Results: An Analytical Perspective on Three Global Challenges Through the Lens of Project Management
summary: This independent analytical paper examines three major global challenges: biodiversity protection, the future of work in the age of artificial intelligence, and global supply chain resilience. Through the lens of project management, the paper explores the gap between global commitments and effective implementation, the unequal distribution of opportunities and resources, and the importance of accountability, education, and human empowerment. It argues that meaningful progress should be measured not only by stated goals, technological advances, or economic indicators, but also by tangible and lasting improvements in people's lives and opportunities. The paper reflects the author's personal perspective and applies project management principles to the analysis of complex global challenges.

title: Capability-Aware Digital Transformation: Adaptive Deployment Strategies for Enterprise AI
summary: A Falsifiable Multidimensional Policy for Sequencing, Capacity-Building, and Reversible Rollout / Enterprise AI implementation increasingly depends on organizational capabilities, governance, and behavior, but these requirements are already recognized in organizational readiness and phased-rollout research. This paper proposes the Capability-Aware Deployment Policy (CADP) as a bounded, testable method rather than a demonstrated technology. CADP represents each enterprise unit through task-specific capability, process, governance, support, benefit, risk, and observed-outcome variables, and uses a transparent policy to choose among capacity-building, pilot, expansion, maintenance, suspension, and rollback. It distinguishes mandatory noncompensatory constraints from soft objectives, explicitly protects safe low-readiness units from automatic exclusion, and accounts for measurement error, intervention overhead, irreversible consequences, and resource contention. A four-policy comparison contrasts simultaneous deployment, fixed staged rollout, technology-readiness ordering, and CADP, with an expert-governed fixed strategy as the strongest practical challenger. The proposed research program specifies adversarial synthetic environments, ablation tests, outcomes for sustained effective adoption, and a conditional prospective cluster evaluation. No simulation, organizational intervention, empirical uplift, algorithmic superiority, or global novelty is reported. The candidate contribution is an independently reproducible policy and falsification contract that will be valuable only if it adds measurable decision quality beyond existing readiness assessments, dynamic treatment methods, and well-designed staged deployment.

title: RaagaReboot: scaling sacred music in India’s digital economy
summary: Learning outcomes After completing the case preparation and participating in the classroom discussion, learners will be able to: Case overview/synopsis This teaching case examines the strategic and ethical challenges faced by RaagaReboot Technologies Pvt. Ltd., a Bengaluru-based cultural media startup navigating the high-stakes intersection of digital innovation and traditional heritage. Founded in late 2023, the startup set out to revitalize interest in regional devotional content among India’s massive Gen Z demographic by adapting traditional musical forms into bite-sized, algorithm-friendly audio-visual experiences for platforms like Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Spotify and JioSaavn. The tension centres on the company’s reinterpretation of Daasa Sahitya, a highly revered devotional literary-musical tradition originating from Karnataka’s Haridasa movement. By layer-packing centuries-old classical compositions with contemporary lo-fi soundscapes, EDM percussion and modern animations, RaagaReboot generated rapid digital virality. However, this growth triggered a severe cultural backlash. A coalition of classical musicians, temple trustees, and cultural scholars formally accused the firm of stripping sacred compositions of their ritual sanctity, melodic (raga) integrity and philosophical depth for the sake of platform monetization. The narrative reaches a critical juncture in August 2026. Founder and CEO Aarav Kulkarni faces a high-pressure boardroom dilemma: he has less than 24 h to secure a crucial ₹2.5 crore seed funding round from a digital entertainment investor. The investor is highly drawn to the platform’s exceptional user metrics but has explicitly conditioned the capital injection on the company’s ability to demonstrate scalable growth without sustained public controversy. Aarav must make a definitive choice: Will he build a disruptive digital media empire at the cost of alienating his own cultural community, or protect the sacred traditions and risk losing the very investors needed to keep his startup alive? Ultimately, this case serves as a live testing ground for postgraduate and executive learners to debate stakeholder salience, the economic power of platform algorithms and the structural design of responsible innovation in highly sensitive market environments. Complexity academic level This teaching case is explicitly designed for postgraduate, Master of Business Administration (MBA), and executive education learners operating within emerging market contexts. Given the complex intersection of digital platform economics, cultural commercialization and stakeholder conflict, the case requires mature analytical capabilities and is not intended for introductory undergraduate levels. The case is uniquely positioned for classroom discussion environments that emphasize strategic decision-making under conditions of ethical ambiguity and rapid technological disruption. Subject code CSS 11: Strategy.

title: Independent Commissioners, Audit Committee, Ownership Structure, and Financial Statement Quality of Indonesian Consumer Cyclicals Firms
summary: This study examines associations between Good Corporate Governance (GCG) mechanisms and financial statement quality in Indonesian consumer cyclicals companies during 2022–2025, controlling for Return on Assets (ROA). Signed Discretionary Accruals (DA) indicate the direction of abnormal accrual adjustments rather than overall reporting quality. Purposive sampling yielded 19 companies and 76 firm-year observations. DA were estimated using the modified Jones model and analyzed through fixed-effects panel regression with Heteroskedasticity-Consistent Standard Errors, Type 1 (HC1) robust standard errors. Independent commissioners (β = 0.047787, p = 0.7227), audit committee meetings (β = −0.010318, p = 0.4797), and institutional ownership (β = −0.003788, p = 0.9574) showed insignificant associations. Managerial ownership was positively associated with DA (β = 0.430569, p = 0.0271), contrary to expectations. ROA was also positively associated (β = 0.562850, p = 0.0032). Although the overall model was significant (p = 0.002878, R² = 0.527732), the joint governance test was insignificant (p = 0.219619). Thus, H1–H5 were unsupported. Governance mechanisms did not consistently constrain income-increasing accrual adjustments. Positive signed DA does not independently establish manipulation or declining reporting quality. Findings are restricted by the sector-specific sample, four-year observation period, and accrual-model assumptions. This study provides sector-specific evidence challenging uniform agency-theory expectations and demonstrates why governance indicators alone cannot establish monitoring effectiveness.

title: Infection–Mortality Dissociation: An Audit of How Global Health Accounting Failed Mycoplasma pneumoniae
summary: Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) infects tens of millions of children in an epidemic year, yet registers as a rounding error in the mortality metrics by which global health allocates resources. We audited this invisibility by triangulating three evidence streams: six national and multinational surveillance systems; a M. pneumoniae–specific secondary analysis of Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 data; and GBD-derived counterfactual projections of the 2023 resurgence extrapolated from pre-pandemic epidemic cycles. Under non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs), MP disappeared more completely and for longer than influenza or RSV; it returned along a policy-timed interval gradient — 6–7 months after NPI relaxation in China, 21–22 months in Japan — exceeding the no-COVID counterfactual projection by 19.2%, breaching its upper prediction interval. Modeled MP mortality in children aged 0–19 years (26,382 deaths, 95% uncertainty interval (UI) 18,984–36,012; ninth of 26 modeled lower respiratory infection (LRI) etiologies) concentrated where measurement is absent: 81.6% of estimated deaths in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, while infections peak at school ages where death is rarest — an infection–mortality dissociation that no single instrument of global health accounting can see. Chronic sequelae compound the omission: bronchiolitis obliterans developed in 7.3% of the largest post-pneumonia follow-up cohort, converting a survivable infection into decades of disability invisible to mortality-weighted metrics. The 2023–2024 resurgence was not an anomaly but an audit finding — a structural failure of measurement, not of biology. We propose five corrections with named institutional owners: MP-specific sentinel surveillance, sequelae-weighted burden metrics, resistance-stewardship infrastructure, diagnostic adoption standards, and vaccine prioritization.

title: Fintech Utilisation, Financial Literacy, Financial Behaviour, Digital Literacy, and MSME Financial Performance
summary: This study examines the relationships of financial technology (fintech) usage, financial literacy, financial behaviour, and digital literacy with the financial performance of culinary micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Larangan District, Tangerang City, Indonesia. It further compares application-oriented capabilities, represented by fintech usage and financial behaviour, with knowledge-oriented capabilities, represented by financial literacy and digital literacy, in relation to financial performance. The study is motivated by the rapid digital transformation of MSMEs and increasing efforts to strengthen their financial and digital capabilities to support business sustainability. Despite these developments, improved access to financial technology and greater financial and digital knowledge do not necessarily correspond to better financial outcomes. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 84 culinary MSME owners selected through purposive sampling. Eligible respondents had operated their businesses for at least one year, had experience using fintech services for business-related activities, and had access to formal financial services. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analysed through multiple linear regression. The results indicate that fintech usage and financial behaviour are positively and significantly associated with MSME financial performance, whereas financial literacy and digital literacy show no statistically significant direct associations. Within the sampled fintech-using culinary MSMEs, application-oriented capabilities therefore show stronger empirical relevance to financial performance than knowledge-oriented capabilities. These findings highlight the importance of complementing financial and digital knowledge with practical financial behaviour and effective technology utilisation in routine business activities.

title: The functional metamorphosis of financial reports: From retrospective model to real-time predictive analytics
summary: Financial reports were designed as periodic, historical-cost records that summarize past transactions for external users. Empirical accounting research has shown both the value and the limits of this model, while advances in statistical modeling, machine learning and data infrastructure have raised expectations for timely, forward-looking information. This article develops a conceptual account of that shift as a three-stage functional change: from a retrospective record, through an analytical-predictive tool, to a real-time predictive information service. Using a structured, qualitative synthesis of foundational and recent peer-reviewed studies and one leading monograph, it proposes a layered reference architecture for real-time predictive reporting and identifies governance, assurance and data-quality conditions for reliable use. The argument is conceptual and does not rely on new empirical data.

title: ALIGNING THE ACCOUNTING OF INSURANCE SERVICES IN INSURANCE COMPANIES WITH INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS
summary: This thesis discusses the theoretical and practical aspects of aligning the accounting of insurance services in insurance companies with the requirements of international standards. It highlights the importance of International Financial Reporting Standards in ensuring the transparency, reliability, and comparability of financial statements in insurance activities. Furthermore, it focuses on developing proposals and recommendations for improving the accounting of insurance services based on international standards, enhancing accounting policies, and improving the quality of financial reporting.

title: Cognitive knowledge architectures in sustainable supply chains: pathways to organizational performance
summary: Purpose Supply chain dynamic capability offers significant potential, yet many organizations struggle to leverage it effectively. Grounded in the resource-based view (RBV), this study aims to investigate how organizations leverage sustainable supply chain practices through knowledge-based resources to improve both sustainable performance and human resource (HR) performance. Design/methodology/approach A total of 412 managers and employees from medium and large manufacturing organizations in China were surveyed, and the partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed framework for evaluating sustainable practices and dynamic capacities to ensure success in challenging times. Findings Findings indicate that sustainable supply chain management practices exert significant positive effects on both sustainable performance and HR performance. Knowledge sharing and knowledge acquisition partially mediate these relationships, serving as complementary knowledge-based resources that translate sustainability practices into performance outcomes. Practical implications The findings of the study equip policymakers and supply chain managers of manufacturing organizations to provide insights on how to integrate knowledge, enhance decision-making and adopt sustainable operations to enhance the success and sustainability of the operations. Originality/value The study contributes to the literature by extending the RBV and highlighting the strategic significance of knowledge-related antecedents to sustainability objectives. It opens the black box of how sustainable supply chain management practices drive organizational performance.

title: Digital Transformation in Entrepreneurship: Implications for Innovation and SME Performance
summary: Digital transformation important role in promoting entrepreneurship, innovation, and the performance of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This study reviews existing literature to examine how digital technologies influence business innovation and organisational outcomes. Technologies include digital platforms, information and communication technology, and automation can support process improvement, customer engagement, and innovative business models. The review draws on perspective to explain how digital resources, managerial competencies, and organisational adaptability contribute to business performance. Digital transformation can improve operational efficiency, competitiveness, and responsiveness to changing market conditions. However, SMEs often face challenges, including financial constraints, inadequate infrastructure, limited digital skills, and resistance to organisational change. These barriers may reduce the effectiveness of technology adoption. The review highlights the importance of strategic planning, employee development, and collaborative networks in strengthening digital capabilities. Overall, successful digital transformation requires integrating technology with organisational objectives and innovation strategies. The findings offer useful insights for entrepreneurs, managers, and policymakers seeking to enhance SME competitiveness and sustainable business development.

title: Bridging the Sustainability Reporting Implementation Gap in an EU Candidate Country: Evidence from Large Companies and Accounting Professionals in Albania
summary: The growing importance of sustainability reporting has transformed corporate reporting practices across Europe, particularly following the adoption of the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). As a candidate country for European Union membership, Albania is expected to progressively align its regulatory and reporting framework with these emerging sustainability reporting requirements. Furthermore, certain categories of entities are already subject to non-financial reporting obligations under the Albanian accounting framework, increasing the relevance of assessing current implementation capacity. However, limited empirical evidence exists regarding the extent to which Albanian companies and accounting professionals are prepared to support this transition. This study investigates the sustainability reporting implementation gap in Albania by examining both corporate reporting practices and professional preparedness. The research adopts a dual empirical approach. First, the study analyses the public reporting practices of the 200 largest Albanian companies identified according to the annual ranking published by Monitor Magazine. Second, the study draws upon survey evidence collected from 127 accounting professionals, including approved accountants, financial reporting specialists, consultants and company representatives. Preliminary findings reveal a substantial implementation gap between emerging sustainability reporting requirements and current reporting practices. While more than 90% of the analysed companies publicly disclose financial statements, sustainability-related disclosures remain extremely limited and largely descriptive in nature. Although many companies publish activity reports, management reports and other non-financial disclosures, the reporting of measurable environmental, social and governance (ESG) indicators is largely absent. The survey findings further indicate limited familiarity among accounting professionals with ESG concepts, sustainability reporting standards and related regulatory requirements. Only a small proportion of respondents reported practical experience in preparing sustainability-related reports, while most professionals did not consider themselves adequately prepared to support sustainability reporting implementation. The study concludes that despite increasing regulatory expectations and Albania’s ongoing alignment with European sustainability reporting requirements, significant challenges remain regarding corporate reporting practices and professional capacity. The findings highlight the need for targeted regulatory guidance, professional training, educational reforms and stronger institutional support to facilitate Albania’s transition towards sustainability reporting in line with European requirements.

title: Indirect tax accountability as record agreement: inventory accounting and auditing under digital technologies and big data
summary: An industrial enterprise keeps three accounts of the same goods. Operations hold a physical record of what moved, the enterprise system holds a transactional record of what was documented and priced, and the tax function holds a fiscal record of what was declared. Indirect taxation works to the extent that the three records agree. The standard evasion schemes in manufacturing, namely unrecorded output, invented purchasing, disguised disposal and elastic valuation, all drive the records apart while leaving each one internally plausible. Serialized marking, sensor networks, enterprise event logs and clearance-model electronic invoicing have changed what can be tested, because the three records now exist at population scale and in machine-readable form. Drawing on tax compliance economics, big data research in auditing, continuous assurance and organizational capability theory, this article reconstructs indirect tax accountability as a property of agreement among the three records rather than of any one of them. It first states the conditions under which agreement is evidence at all. A reconciliation carries weight only where its two sides descend from causally separate processes, so the records must contain measurement anchors generated outside the enterprise transaction-processing layer. Integrated systems violate that condition by default. Agreement is then formalized as a set of reconciliation residuals, and a detection condition is derived from stated assumptions. A scheme survives only while its divergence stays inside the noise floor of the tightest independent check that sees it, so the sustainable tax gap is the sum of those noise floors rather than a function of the number of controls in place. A sensitivity analysis shows how the bound moves when the assumptions of separability, exogenous tolerances and zero detection risk are relaxed. Four leakage channels are traced through the inventory cycle, matched to the reconciliation that exposes each, and condensed into four propositions with refuting observations and candidate measures. Uzbekistan is the instantiating setting, where clearance invoicing, serialized labeling and, from January 2026, automated invoice risk scoring have outrun enterprise capability, and where documented administrative reconciliation practice between 2021 and 2023 supplies a live episode and its governance failure mode.

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Government Financial Reporting Transparency: Evidence from Nigeria's Federal Public Sector
summary: Transparency is widely expected to sustain public trust in government, and artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed as a means of making public financial information more open, timely and understandable. This study examines whether the overall level of documented AI adoption is associated with the transparency of government financial reporting in Nigeria's federal public sector, and what the evidence implies for public trust. A balanced panel of five federal institutions: the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, the Federal Inland Revenue Service, the Central Bank of Nigeria and the Bureau of Public Procurement were observed from 2015 to 2024. Documentary evidence from annual reports, audit-related documents and AI-implementation documents is scored on a five-point (0–4) rubric and analysed with pooled, fixed-effects, trend-adjusted, first-difference and lagged regressions, interpreted through agency theory. Overall AI adoption is positively and significantly associated with transparency and credibility of financial reports (pooled β = 0.701, R² = 0.810; fixed-effects β = 0.708). Unlike the study's other AI–outcome relationships, however, this one is not robust throughout: the trend-adjusted coefficient (0.616) is only marginally significant (p = 0.051), and the first-difference coefficient (0.604) is not statistically significant (p = 0.112), although the lagged estimate (0.599) is. Transparency also has the lowest mean score of the five outcomes. The outcome is a documentary score of openness and credibility, not a survey of citizens, so the results speak to the supply of transparency and cannot establish public trust itself. Because the design is observational, the measures are documentary indices, and the sample is small and purposively selected, the results indicate association rather than proven causation and are interpreted for the five institutions examined rather than for all federal ministries, departments and agencies. AI adoption appears to be a helpful but insufficient condition for transparent reporting; communication, civic capacity and audit validation matter too.

title: IMPACT OF CLOUD AUDITING ON IMPROVING AUDIT QUALITY
summary: This study examines the impact of cloud auditing on audit quality improvement through an applied study of a sample of auditors. This study addresses the growing adoption of cloud computing in accounting and auditing environments and the need to assess its contribution to audit procedures’ efficiency and quality of audit procedures. This study focuses on the role of cloud auditing in facilitating access to audit data, enhancing information security and data protection, supporting data integrity and availability, improving the efficiency of cloud-auditing procedures, and managing risks associated with the cloud environment. The study adopts a descriptive-analytical approach and relies on a questionnaire administered to a sample of auditors. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, Pearson correlation, and regression analysis to examine the relationship between cloud auditing and audit quality. This study seeks to determine whether the use of cloud-based auditing practices improves the quality of the audit process and enhances the effectiveness and efficiency of auditors’ performance. The findings of this study indicate that cloud auditing has a positive relationship with audit quality and that the adoption of cloud-based technologies can support auditors in obtaining and processing audit evidence more efficiently while strengthening data protection and risk-management practices. The study recommends enhancing auditors’ professional and technical knowledge of cloud auditing, strengthening information security controls, and developing appropriate procedures for managing risks associated with cloud-based audit environments

title: Accounting skills, auditor independence, and internal audit effectiveness: Evidence from a provincial inspectorate in Indonesia
summary: Weak internal control and recurring audit findings in Indonesian local governments raise questions about how effective internal audit is in the public sector. Drawing on agency theory and stewardship theory, this study examines the effect of internal auditors’ accounting skills and independence on internal audit effectiveness at the Regional Inspectorate of North Sulawesi Province. An explanatory quantitative design was applied, using a questionnaire on a four-point Likert scale distributed to all internal auditors of the Government Internal Supervisory Apparatus (total sampling); 63 usable responses were analyzed with multiple linear regression. The results show that accounting skills and independence each have a positive and significant effect on internal audit effectiveness, and that both variables jointly have a significant effect. Independence is the stronger predictor, and the model explains a substantial share of the variation in audit effectiveness. This study contributes by isolating accounting skills, rather than general auditor competence, and by providing evidence from a provincial inspectorate, where research remains scarce. The findings imply that the Inspectorate should strengthen accounting-specific competency development and protect auditors from intervention. The results should be read with caution because the data come from a single institution, rely on respondents’ perceptions, and exclude auditors who did not respond.

title: Financial development and the energy transition in China: Does green capital accelerate decarbonization?
summary: China's dual carbon targets peak CO2 by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060 place financial markets at the centre of the country's clean energy transition. This paper investigates whether financial development, and green finance in particular, accelerates decarbonization across China's 30 provinces over the period 2003 to 2022. A composite Financial Development Index (FDI) is constructed using principal component analysis from four dimensions: banking sector depth, stock market development, insurance market penetration, and green finance intensity (green credit ratio and green bond issuance). The analysis employs a two-way fixed-effects spatial Durbin model (SDM) with a queen-contiguity weight matrix to capture spatial spillovers, a double-threshold panel regression to identify nonlinear green finance effects, and a bootstrap mediation analysis to decompose transmission channels. Results demonstrate that a one-standard-deviation increase in the composite FDI reduces provincial CO2 emissions by 21.8% (direct effect) and generates a cross-provincial spillover reduction of 9.6%, for a total effect of 31.4%. Green finance exhibits the strongest individual sub-component effect, reducing emissions by 28.4% and displaying threshold behaviour: the decarbonization impact is insignificant below a green finance intensity ratio of 0.32, rises sharply in the intermediate regime (0.32 to 0.62), and intensifies further above 0.62 as capital allocation shifts systematically toward renewable energy and low-carbon technology. Mediation analysis identifies four significant channels technology innovation, renewable energy investment, industrial ecology upgrading, and energy efficiency improvement which together account for 21.3% of the total effect. Regional heterogeneity analysis reveals that the green finance channel is strongest in Eastern provinces, where capital markets are deepest, and weakest in Western provinces, suggesting a financial geography constraint on clean transition. The findings imply that accelerating green bond market development, expanding the green credit incentive framework, and closing cross-provincial financial integration gaps are essential policy levers for meeting the 2030 peak-emissions deadline.

title: Digital Economy and Tax Administration Reform: Research Progress and Prospects
summary: Due to the constant updating and the new version of digital technologies, the digital economy has now become one of the main engines of China’s high-quality development. Simultaneously, the tax administration system is at the most crucial point of reform and is the subject of intensive study by researchers. The present paper is an attempt to review the digital economy and tax administration and their connection by analyzing and reviewing the literature that was obtained in CNKI during 2020-2026. It is found that the digital economy strongly impacts tax administration, and the aim is to identify some challenges faced by tax administration, so as to give some suggestions to the later studies related to the topic. The current literature is missing any systematic review and synthesis of the two; further studies should be conducted on cross-validation using various methods and choosing diversified data.
